reason: A length comparison with a named second part ('longer than or equaling the perigynium'); 'slightly' is a qualifier kept in RDF and 'or equaling' is an alternative (pattern 07/10).
Hair-shaped (capillary) culms, stems and blades are very slender and thread-like, which is the existing PATO filiform.

target: new: depth of division (calyx limb FLOPO_0986093 + split PATO_0001786, depth as a fraction of the limb, docs/odp/10-ratio-to-another-part.md)
reason: The bearer is the existing calyx limb class and the quality is split. 'to base', '1/2' and '9/10' give how deep the division goes, which is a ratio and not a term.
Halfway between erect and spreading. This follows the earlier rule for 'erect-spreading', which went to PATO_0002260.

target: new: gradient along a series (decreased size PATO_0000587 of the members towards the apex)
reason: The pinnae or leaflets get smaller towards the tip of the blade. That describes a position in a series, not one value of a single part. Where only the apex outline is meant, 'gradually narrowed' already goes to tapered (PATO_0001500).
Crenulate is an EXACT synonym of PATO scalloped. 'Irregularly' is a manner qualifier, handled the same way as 'irregularly rectangular' → rectangular.
Covered with bristle-like hairs is the existing PATO bristly. 'Hairy' adds nothing.
Like parts (calyx, involucel or perianth members) fused together. This matches the earlier rules for gamopetalous and gamosepalous.
The pedicel is included towards a second part, the ocrea or ocreola. PO has no ocrea class, so the second part stays as words until one exists.
Erect but diverging at a small angle. Same rule as 'erect-spreading'. For paired thecae, divergence from each other would be a relation (pattern 09) where it is stated so.
One ovule is a count of ovules. The same decision was made earlier for 'uniovulate'.
A compound of two shape values, handled by the continuum relation in the same way as 'campanulate-turbinate'.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (part of the bearer: leaf midvein PO_0020139 + conspicuous PATO_0000463)
reason: A part plus a quality in one phrase: the midrib (synonym of leaf midvein) is clearly visible. This follows the rule 'veins distinct' → conspicuous.

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md (inserted just below the calyx PO_0009060)
reason: Bracteoles 'subcalicinales' sit just beneath the calyx, which is a position relative to another part. The bare 'flowers subcalycine' is unclear and should stay in review.

label: amentiform
definition: A spike-like quality inhering in an inflorescence by virtue of its being a dense, slender, often pendulous spike of small, inconspicuous, usually unisexual flowers, resembling a catkin.
reason: Like spike-like and raceme-like, this means 'resembling', so it is not the catkin inflorescence class (PO_0030119). The label avoids 'catkin-like', which is already a synonym of julaceous (FLOPO:0991232), a leafy-shoot quality.
A compound of two 3-D shape values, handled like 'ellipsoid-ovoid' and 'ovoid-elliptic'.
The negation of the existing FLOPO bullate, as 'non-resupinate' was handled.
Prognathous means jutting forward like a jaw, here of an orifice, anther or thecae. PATO protruding is the nearest existing term. The sense differs between families, so the records should be checked.
A generic pit or depression (on petiole, glume, seed or disk) that needs the organ it belongs to, like 'pit' and 'depression' in the earlier reviews. The bare surface reading would be foveate.
A compound of two shape values, handled by the continuum relation like 'linear-elliptic'.
'In outline' only says that the shape word that goes with it is a 2-D shape. The quality is that shape word (orbicular, oval), not 'outline'.
Vague without context. It is used for buttresses, thallus flanks, annuli and grooves in unrelated senses (slope, angle of a wall), and has no single quality reading.
A lower glume that is cuff-like is reduced to a short collar or rim round the base of the spikelet, which is ring-shaped (annular).
A spelling variant of the existing FLOPO tubercle-based. The bearer is the hairs (trichome PO_0000282), not the organ that carries them.
'Foliar bracts' and 'sepals ± foliar' mean leaf-like, as in the earlier rule for foliaceous. Only the qualifying use should be mapped, not the 'of the leaf' sense.
This follows the earlier rule for 'rooting'. 'At the lower nodes' is the position of the roots on the stem (pattern 18) and 'often' or 'sometimes' are frequencies kept in RDF.
The second-model review read 'striation' as the quality striated of the part that bears it. 'Without striations' is the negated form, and counts go by pattern 03.

Tomentulose is finely or shortly tomentose. 'Densely' is a degree qualifier, as 'sparsely pubescent' → pubescent. A diminutive class like puberulous could come later if tomentulose shows up on its own often enough.
A nidular inflorescence (Bromeliaceae) sits deep in the centre of the leaf rosette and does not reach beyond it, which is the existing FLOPO included towards the rosette leaves.
A transcription of 'sparingly pubescent'. Same rule as 'sparsely pubescent': the density word is a qualifier.
